description: Searches WEM's partner-feed products by meaning, for a plain-language need such as "comfortable shoes for standing all day" or "gift for a 10 year old who likes science". If the description is a product identifier (a barcode, ASIN, MPN, merchant SKU or wem3.ai/pl URL), that product is looked up instead and the reply takes the keyword-search shape. When no products come back, `reason` says why: `index_empty` means nothing matched; `no_embedding_key`, `no_catalogue_client`, `embedding_failed`, `query_failed` and `timed_out` mean the semantic index could not be searched this time, which says nothing about whether such products exist.

category.description: Optional. Keeps only products whose feed category matches this text exactly.

description.description: Plain-language description of what the shopper needs.

max_price.description: Optional upper price bound, compared with each product's listed price (currencies are not converted).

min_price.description: Optional lower price bound, compared with each product's listed price (currencies are not converted).

provider.description: Optional. Keeps only products from this partner feed, e.g. "awin".

name: semantic_search

outputSchema.description: Empty when the vector path cannot rank (`semantic: false`), with `reason` naming which cause applies — they have different fixes, so do not read them all as an empty index. `semantic` is true only when pgvector actually ranked products.

catalogMatch.description: Offers WEM holds under one catalogue product. Check `identityBasis`: on `barcode` the product carries a GTIN and every offer here is that same item, so prefer them and cite their prices over anything in `products`. On `curated-grouping` the product carries no barcode, the grouping is an inference like any title match, and a cheaper row in `products` may well be the same item — see `cheaperElsewhere`. Whether the shopper’s words reached this product by barcode or by name is `identity`, a separate question: on `inferred`, say WEM matched it by name.

cheaperElsewhere.description: Present only on a `curated-grouping` block that a live row in `products` undercuts. WEM is telling you its own catalogue block is not the best price it found. Quote this row as the cheaper option with its identity stated as unconfirmed; never present the catalogMatch price as the lowest when this is set.

identity.description: Always `inferred` — matched on title, not barcode. Say so when quoting it.

savingVsCatalogue.description: How much cheaper this row is than the block’s lowest offer.

identity.description: How the shopper’s words reached this product. On `inferred`, WEM matched it by name (not by barcode) and the identity is not confirmed, even when `identityBasis` is `barcode`; on `exact`, the barcode itself resolved it.

strength.description: exact = barcode; catalogued = a WEM key or listing id; inferred = matched on the product name, MPN or SKU and still a guess.

identityBasis.description: What this block’s identity rests on. `barcode` — the canonical product carries a GTIN and these offers are the same physical item. `curated-grouping` — it carries none, so the grouping is an inference of the same kind a title match is; do not describe it to the user as barcode-confirmed, and do not let it outrank a cheaper row in `products` on price alone. This is how the offers are grouped, not how the query matched the product — see `identity`.

lastConfirmedAt.description: When WEM last actually read any price in this block. Null means none of them can be dated — say so rather than implying the block is current.

lowPrice.description: Lowest CURRENT price in `offers` (priceStatus `current`). Null when none is current: never fill it from an older or undated row.

affiliate.description: False when this link earns WEM nothing: the shop has no affiliate programme with WEM, or this link does not carry one. It is still a real offer, and its link is not affiliate-tracked. Absent (or true) means the link is affiliate-tracked. `disclosure` states whether all, some or none of the links are tracked.

channel.description: retailer is a named shop (Boots, Currys). marketplace is eBay/AliExpress/Temu-style parallel listings. A marketplace cluster is not a set of competing authorised retailers.

lastSeenAt.description: When WEM last READ this price from the retailer or a datafeed — the same reading `priceAgeDays` counts from, so the two always agree. Null means WEM cannot date the price: it is undated, not current.

price.description: Indicative price. The retailer sets the final price at checkout. Null, with `priceNote`, when WEM may not show this listing’s price: the note stands in place of a figure.

priceAgeDays.description: Calendar days (UK time) since WEM last READ this price: 0 read today, 1 yesterday. Null means WEM cannot say. Null is undated, not current.

priceNote.description: Present only when `price` is null: the words that stand in its place, e.g. "See price at Amazon". An Amazon price is shown only when Amazon’s API supplied it just now.

priceQualifier.description: Present when `price` is the OPENING price of a range, not the price of this item: a multi-variation listing where the seller advertises its cheapest variant and the shopper picks a size on the page. It reads as "from £X"; it is not the item's price or the cheapest. Absent means the price is firm for the row as described.

priceRefresh.description: What re-reads this retailer’s prices: `live-api` a product-lookup API, `feed` a partner datafeed, `none` nothing on a schedule. `none` means the figure will not move on its own however long it sits ; `priceAgeDays` dates it.

priceStatus.description: `current`: WEM read this price within the last 14 days; only a current price may lead, be called the cheapest or lowest, be compared or enter a saving. `stale`: read longer ago. `undated`: WEM cannot say when. Those two read as "last seen £X on 8 Sep" or "price not dated", come after the current ones, and are not compared. Absent on a row a provider answered just now.

shipping.description: Delivery as the retailer stated it: `free`, or `cost` in the offer currency. Absent or null means not stated: say delivery is shown at the shop, never that it is free. Offers are ordered by item price; add a stated cost before calling one cheaper delivered.

estimate.description: Delivery window when the feed stated one.

unitPrice.description: Price per 100ml, 100g, litre, kg or item, from the size this row's title states. Present only when the rows differ in size, in one unit across all of them, and only for things bought by the amount (beauty, food, supplements), never an appliance's capacity. Across sizes, value is compared on these, not on the prices: a smaller size is not cheaper because its price is lower. It reads beside the price ("£29.95, £99.83 per 100ml"). Absent does not mean the price is per unit.

url.description: WEM tracked link to the retailer page for this offer. WEM never takes payment.

verified.description: True when WEM has recently observed this price on the retailer’s own surface. False means the identity is still catalogue-resolved but the price is indicative (partner feed or stale) — do not present it as verified.

unpriced.description: Listings whose price WEM may not show — today, Amazon rows Amazon’s API did not price just now. The row carries `priceNote` (e.g. "See price at Amazon") in place of a figure. No price is stated, estimated or compared for one; it is not the cheapest and is not counted in a lowest price or a saving.

priceNote.description: What stands where a price would be, e.g. "See price at Amazon".

url.description: WEM tracked link. The full URL; a shortened form is a different link.

disclosure.description: WEM’s affiliate disclosure for this answer, written to be quoted as it is. Its wording changes with the rows: it states whether every outbound link is affiliate-tracked, only some are, or none are. A version from an earlier answer may not fit this one: a row marked `affiliate: false` earns WEM nothing.

filtered.description: Withheld candidates tallied by reason (e.g. accessories, another model, a bundle or multipack, a replica, a listing priced far below the product’s other offers). Report this count rather than implying the search was exhaustive, and never quote a withheld listing’s price as the cheapest or as a deal.

next.description: Present when WEM's set of offers is thin. chrome_extension is a page that compares the same product on any retailer page, including shops without an affiliate programme.

affiliate.description: False when this link earns WEM nothing: the shop has no affiliate programme with WEM, or this link does not carry one. It is still a real offer, and its link is not affiliate-tracked. Absent (or true) means the link is affiliate-tracked. `disclosure` states whether all, some or none of the links are tracked.

channel.description: retailer is a named shop (Boots, Currys). marketplace is eBay/AliExpress/Temu-style parallel listings. A marketplace cluster is not a set of competing authorised retailers.

price.description: Indicative price. The retailer sets the final price at checkout. Null, with `priceNote`, when WEM may not show this listing’s price: the note stands in place of a figure.

priceNote.description: Present only when `price` is null: the words that stand in its place, e.g. "See price at Amazon". An Amazon price is shown only when Amazon’s API supplied it just now.

priceQualifier.description: Present when `price` is the OPENING price of a range, not the price of this item: a multi-variation listing where the seller advertises its cheapest variant and the shopper picks a size on the page. It reads as "from £X"; it is not the item's price or the cheapest. Absent means the price is firm for the row as described.

Those two read as "last seen £X on 8 Sep" or "price not dated", come after the current ones, and are not compared. Absent on a row a provider answered just now.

Present only when the rows differ in size, in one unit across all of them, and only for things bought by the amount (beauty, food, supplements), never an appliance's capacity. Across sizes, value is compared on these, not on the prices: a smaller size is not cheaper because its price is lower. It reads beside the price ("£29.95, £99.83 per 100ml"). Absent does not mean the price is per unit.

url.description: WEM tracked link to the retailer page for this offer. WEM never takes payment.

reason.description: Present when semantic is false, and never a judgement on the shopper query. `index_empty` — the vector query ran and matched nothing. `no_catalogue_client` / `no_embedding_key` — WEM is misconfigured, not the catalogue empty. `embedding_failed` / `query_failed` — an upstream call failed; retrying later may succeed. `timed_out` — an upstream call did not answer in time; this says nothing about the catalogue.

search.description: Present when this result names no offer. `url` is WEM's results page for the query and `markdown` is the same link, pre-formatted. WEM searches retailers live on that page, including shops it holds no affiliate programme with, so an empty or withheld result here is not evidence the product is unavailable or unpriced.

semantic.description: True only when the vector path actually ran.

title: Find products by description
